ledger.x: 1422: the Livonian lands stand apart from the Teutonic Order.
4 December 1435: the Livonian Confederation agreement is signed at Walk.
1558: Dorpat and Narva fall to the Russians.
31 August 1559: the first Treaty of Vilnius puts Livonia under Polish-Lithuanian protection.
26 September 1559: the Bishop of Ösel-Wiek sells to Denmark.
28 November 1561: the Livonian Order is secularised and Livonia passes to Poland-Lithuania.
28 November 1561: Courland and Semigallia become Kettler's duchy under Poland-Lithuania.
28 November 1561: the Confederation ceases to exist, so its fight with Russia ends here.
28 November 1561: the Confederation ceases to exist, so its fight with Russia over Fellin ends with it (as for Dorpat and Narva, previous event).
28 November 1561: the protection ends with the second Treaty of Vilnius ('The Treaty of Vilnius was concluded on 28 November 1561'; the page does not say in so many words that the protection ended).

wars.name: Russo-Livonian War (1501-1503)
wars.outcome: Plettenberg won the Battle of Lake Smolina on 13 September 1502; after the defeat at Helme and the failed siege of Pskov 'peace between Ivan III and Livonia on the terms of status quo ante bellum was concluded' in 1503 (a six-year truce, renewed 1509, 1521…

wars.name: Livonian War
wars.outcome: The Livonian Confederation was partitioned in 1559-1561 (the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek to Denmark-Norway, Fellin to Russia 1560, Estonia to Sweden, Livonia, Courland and Semigallia to Poland-Lithuania); the war ran to the Truce of Jam Zapolski (1582, Russia lost…

certainty.note: Cliopatria draws the Confederation as whole modern Latvia and Estonia; the lands of the Order, the archbishop and the bishops were intermixed, and the eastern frontier on the Narva and Lake Peipus was fixed only as 'status quo ante bellum'…
A shifting front of the Livonian War; the 28 November 1561 Treaty of Vilnius is a treaty line only on paper.
